sources.title: Learn about rent increases in San Francisco (Topic 050)
sources.summary: Official rules for 1.6% annual allowable increase (3/1/26–2/28/27), Rent Increase License prerequisite, base-rent-only rule, prohibition on rounding up, 12-month anniversary date rules, 30/90-day written notice (+5 days if mailed), prohibition on extra rent for additional roommates, and multi-year anniversary shift examples.

sources.title: Annual Rent Increase for 3/1/26 - 2/28/27 Announced (Jan. 14, 2026)
sources.summary: Official announcement setting 1.6% annual allowable rent increase for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 (and confirming 1.4% for March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026).

sources.agency: San Francisco Rent Board (Official Rate Schedule PDF)
sources.title: Form 571: Allowable Annual Rent Increases (1982–2027)
sources.summary: Complete official historical table of SF Rent Board annual allowable increases from 4/1/82 through 2/28/27, including 2.6% (2019–20), 1.8% (2020–21), 0.7% (2021–22), 2.3% (2022–23), 3.6% (2023–24), 1.7% (2024–25), 1.4% (2025–26), and 1.6% (2026–27).

sources.title: Current Rates, including Rent Increase, Relocation, Security Deposit & Bankable Rent Board Fees
sources.summary: Official schedule of current allowable rent increases (1.6%), security deposit interest (4.2% for 3/1/26–2/28/27), bankable tenant share of Rent Board Fees ($29.50), capital improvement imputed interest rates, and statutory relocation payments.

sources.title: Banked rent increases (Topic 503)
sources.summary: Official rules on banking skipped annual increases: 24 full months must pass without an increase for a skipped year to bank; simple addition of percentages (no compounding or proration); banked amounts do not expire during a tenancy; notice must specify banked portion; license required.

sources.title: Annual rent increase for multiple years
sources.summary: Official Rent Board calculation guide for multi-year rent increases: additive percentages on base rent only, no compounding, no rounding up to nearest dollar, no passthroughs included in base rent, 30-day written notice (+5 days by mail).

sources.title: Learn about San Francisco rental laws (Coverage & June 13, 1979 threshold)
sources.summary: Explains full rent-control and just-cause eviction coverage for multi-unit residential buildings built on or before June 13, 1979, partial exemptions for post-1979 construction and certain single-family/condo units under Costa-Hawkins, and Rent Board counseling.

sources.title: The Rent Board Housing Inventory & Rent Increase License
sources.summary: Mandatory annual Housing Inventory reporting (March 1 deadline; operative July 1, 2022 for 10+ unit buildings and March 1, 2023 for 1–9 unit buildings/condos); bulk Excel upload for 5+ units vs Individual Unit portal form; active Rent Increase License required on effective date for any annual or banked increase to be enforceable.

sources.title: The Rent Board Fee (2026–2027 Tax Year)
sources.summary: Annual Rent Board Fee ($59.00 per dwelling unit for 2026–2027, due March 1); owners who timely pay in full may recover 50% ($29.50) from tenants in occupancy as of November 1, billed separately from base rent without late penalties.

sources.title: Rent Increases Under Section 6.14 And Costa-Hawkins (Topic 153)
sources.summary: Market-rate reset applies ONLY when the last original occupant vacates / no longer permanently resides in the unit. Co-tenants (who have a direct agreement with or pay rent accepted by the landlord) are exempt from Costa-Hawkins increases unless timely served a written Section 6.14 notice.

sources.title: Landlord Petitions and Passthroughs (Topic 301)
sources.summary: Defines the six landlord petition categories (Capital Improvement, Operating & Maintenance, Special Circumstances/Comparable Rents, Prop I, Utility Passthrough, Section 1.21 Tenant in Occupancy) and worksheet-based bond passthroughs required for any increase above annual CPI/banked limits.

sources.title: The California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) — SF Guidance
sources.summary: Confirms AB 1482 state cap for SF (8.8% for Aug. 1, 2026 – July 31, 2027 = 5% + 3.8% CPI) does NOT apply to units governed by stricter SF Rent Ordinance rent-increase limits; notes REITs/corporations/corporate-member LLCs are excluded from single-family/condo exemptions.

sources.title: The Rent Ordinance — Chapter 37, SF Administrative Code (Amended through 11/02/26)
sources.summary: Official Rent Board table of contents and consolidated text index for SF Administrative Code Chapter 37 (Sections 37.1–37.16), updated through November 2, 2026.

sources.title: Form 601: List of Rent Ordinance Amendments through 11/02/26
sources.summary: Chronological log of all SF Rent Ordinance amendments from June 13, 1979 (Ord. 276-79) through October 2, 2026 (Ord. 207-26), including Ord. 224-24 & 169-25 (§ 37.10C algorithmic pricing ban & tenant-org standing) and Ord. 003-26 (§§ 37.2–37.9E).

sources.title: Rent Ordinance Sec. 37.10B — Tenant Harassment
sources.summary: Prohibits bad-faith harassment, coercive rent increases, retaliation, privacy violations, and housing discrimination; provides civil remedies of treble actual damages or $1,000 statutory minimum plus mandatory prevailing-tenant attorney's fees.

sources.title: Algorithmic devices that set rent are prohibited in San Francisco (Sec. 37.10C)
sources.summary: Prohibits landlords from using revenue-management software analyzing non-public competitor data to set rents or occupancy levels in San Francisco; up to $1,000 civil penalty per unit per month plus prevailing-tenant attorney's fees.

sources.title: Update to Algorithmic Devices Law — Tenant Organization Standing (Oct. 6, 2025)
sources.summary: Effective October 6, 2025 (Ord. 169-25), San Francisco tenants' rights organizations have direct statutory standing to file civil lawsuits against landlords violating Section 37.10C.

sources.title: Evictions in San Francisco & Free Legal Help Referral
sources.summary: Outlines 17 just-cause eviction grounds, Rent Board counselor line (415-252-4600), and free tenant legal defense access via Eviction Defense Collaborative (415-659-9184) and the Rent Board Referral Listing.

sources.title: Rent Board Referral Listing (Form 590 — Tenant, Landlord & Legal Clinics)
sources.summary: Official directory of free/low-cost tenant legal & counseling organizations—including Open Door Legal's Sunset Office at 1722 Irving St., ZIP 94122, Eviction Defense Collaborative, Housing Rights Committee, SF Tenants Union, Bay Area Legal Aid, Legal Assistance to the Elderly, and BASF—plus landlord associations (SFAA, SPOSFI).

sources.agency: San Francisco Rent Board (Official Statistical Report PDF)
sources.title: San Francisco Rent Board Annual Statistical Report, FY 2024–2025
sources.summary: Empirical Rent Board filing counts citywide (3,861 total filings; 880 tenant petitions; 339 landlord petitions including 209 Capital Improvement petitions covering 1,261 units and 42 Utility Passthrough Worksheets covering 849 units) and ZIP 94122 (Sunset) counts (42 tenant petitions, 15 Capital Improvement petitions, 14 wrongful eviction reports).

sources.agency: San Francisco Rent Board (Official Annual Buyout Report PDF)
sources.title: 2026 Rent Board Annual Report on Buyout Agreements (Jan. 30, 2026)
sources.summary: Reports calendar-year 2025 Section 37.9E buyout activity by neighborhood, documenting 59 Pre-Buyout Declarations and 36 Buyout Agreements filed in ZIP 94122 (Sunset).

sources.agency: City and County of San Francisco — Housing Trust Fund / MOHCD
sources.title: Housing Trust Fund Five-Year Report (Tenant Right to Counsel — Prop F)
sources.summary: Documents San Francisco's voter-approved No Eviction Without Representation Act (June 2018 Proposition F) establishing the city-funded Tenant Right to Counsel program administered through MOHCD.

sources.title: California Civil Code § 827 — Notice of Change in Terms / Rent Increase
sources.summary: Limits unilateral rent-increase notices to periodic (week-to-week/month-to-month) tenancies; requires 30-day written notice for increases ≤10% (cumulatively over 12 months) and 90-day written notice for increases >10%, served personally or by mail per CCP § 1013.

sources.title: California Code of Civil Procedure § 1013 — Service by Mail (+5 Calendar Days)
sources.summary: Extends statutory notice periods by 5 calendar days when mailed from and addressed within California, requiring notation of date and place of mailing or certificate of mailing.

sources.title: California Civil Code § 1947.12 — Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482)
sources.summary: Establishes statewide rent cap (5% + CPI, max 10%) through Jan. 1, 2030, while exempting units subject to stricter local rent-control ordinances and excluding REITs/corporations from single-family exemptions.

sources.title: California Civil Code § 1954.53 — Costa-Hawkins Vacancy Decontrol & Original Occupants
sources.summary: Authorizes market-rate initial rents on vacant units, but § 1954.53(d)(2)–(3) expressly bars vacancy increases on partial occupancy changes where at least one original occupant pursuant to the rental agreement with the owner remains in lawful possession.

sources.title: California Civil Code § 1942.5 — Prohibition on Retaliatory Rent Increases
sources.summary: Prohibits increasing rent, decreasing services, or evicting within 180 days of a tenant's good-faith habitability complaint or agency citation (§ 1942.5(a)), or at any time in retaliation for peaceably exercising legal rights or tenant organizing (§ 1942.5(d)).

sources.title: California Government Code § 12955 — Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
sources.summary: Prohibits housing discrimination, harassment, discriminatory inquiries/notices, and retaliation across protected classes including race, color, religion, sex, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran/military status, and genetic information.

sources.title: California Civil Rights Department — Fair Housing Protections & Enforcement
sources.summary: Official state enforcement guidance on FEHA and Unruh Civil Rights Act housing protections, including citizenship, immigration status, primary language, age, source of income (vouchers), reasonable accommodations, and associational/perceived traits.

sources.agency: California Office of the Attorney General (oag.ca.gov)
sources.title: AG Bonta & U.S. DOJ Antitrust Lawsuit Against Algorithmic Multifamily Pricing (Aug. 23, 2024)
sources.summary: Documents state and federal antitrust enforcement against corporate landlords and revenue-management software sharing nonpublic pricing/occupancy data to coordinate rent increases and suppress concessions.

sources.agency: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
sources.title: Housing Discrimination Under the Fair Housing Act (42 U.S.C. §§ 3601–3619)
sources.summary: Federal Fair Housing Act overview covering protected classes (race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, disability) and HUD FHEO complaint enforcement; establishes no federal percentage rent-control cap for unsubsidized private rentals.

sources.agency: U.S. Department of Justice — Civil Rights Division
sources.title: Fair Housing Act §§ 3604(b) & 3617 Post-Acquisition Rental Terms & Anti-Retaliation Analysis
sources.summary: Confirms 42 U.S.C. § 3604(b) bars discriminatory terms, conditions, or privileges during an ongoing tenancy (including discriminatory rent terms) and 42 U.S.C. § 3617 bars coercion, intimidation, or retaliation.

sources.agency: U.S. Department of Justice — Antitrust Division
sources.title: Justice Department Sues RealPage for Algorithmic Pricing Scheme in Multifamily Rentals
sources.summary: Documents how large corporate multifamily operators used revenue-management software (YieldStar/AIRM), auto-accept renewal workflows, and concession discipline, triggering Sherman Act §§ 1–2 enforcement.

sources.agency: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development — Office of Policy Development & Research
sources.title: FY 2027 Schedule of Metropolitan Fair Market Rents — San Francisco, CA HMFA (Page 35)
sources.summary: Official FY 2027 40th-percentile Fair Market Rents for San Francisco, CA HMFA: Efficiency $2,574; 1-BR $3,003; 2-BR $3,697; 3-BR $4,832; 4-BR $5,439. Federal voucher benchmark only, not a rent-control authorization.

sources.title: Residential REIT Annual Report on Form 10-K (FY 2025) — Rent Control & Renewal Disclosures
sources.summary: Public REIT Form 10-K disclosure illustrating institutional residential operator tracking of amortized lease renewals, concessions, and compliance risk under California state (AB 1482) and local rent-control ordinances.

sources.summary: Repository history, multi-session coordination log, inherited NBA/NFL sports analytics modules, CI workflows, and peer rental-sf audit baseline.
